#774. Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?

The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Moscow has increasingly relied on a so-called shadow fleet to bypass Western sanctions and transport its oil around the world.

Other heavily sanctioned countries, including Iran and Venezuela, have also been accused of using such vessels to export petroleum products.

These tankers often rely on deceptive practices like turning off their location transponders to evade detection and conceal the cargo's true origins or destinations.

The fleet, which consists largely of aging, uninsured and poorly maintained tankers, has raised widespread concern across the shipping industry. Yet it has expanded rapidly in recent years and now accounts for nearly 19% of global oil tanker capacity, according to estimates by financial intelligence firm S&P Global.

"The shadow fleet is a scourge," Elisabeth Braw, senior fellow at the think tank Atlantic Council, said, adding that "it is in nobody's interest" to have these ships sailing around in the world's oceans.

She pointed out that these tankers undermine the maritime order and increase the risk of accidents and environmental damage.

"Every country should use its leverage with Russia to ask it not to use the fleet," she told DW, noting that ultimately all countries suffer the consequences.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

To clamp down on the fleet and curb Russia's oil export revenues, the United States and European countries have stepped up efforts to intercept tankers accused of violating sanctions.

The Trump administration, however, is reportedly considering lifting sanctions on some shadow fleet vessels and allowing them to transport oil that is not subject to sanctions.

A US official told Reuters earlier this month that the move was intended to ease record-high global freight rates.

Lifting sanctions on the shadow fleet "would decrease the effectiveness of the sanctions regime overall," said Michael Carpenter, senior fellow for Transatlantic Affairs at the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS). Such a move "rewards the aggressor and helps Moscow gain revenues to continue attacking Ukraine," he told DW.

"This is the exact opposite of what the US should be doing if it wants to end the war."

Carpenter, who previously served as US ambassador to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said any sanctions relief would also put the US and the EU "strategically at odds with each other, with the EU clearly backing Ukraine and the US increasingly supporting Russia's financial goals."

This view is shared by Ben Harris, vice president and director of Economic Studies at the Brookings Institution.

Lifting sanctions on shadow fleet tankers would "make it substantially easier for Russia to trade its oil at market rates," he said, pointing out that it would "improve its government finances since so much revenue is tied to energy markets."

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, however, rejected suggestions that the US was removing sanctions from shadow fleet tankers.

"We are converting dark tankers to legitimate tankers," Bloomberg quoted Wright as saying last week. "There is no removing of sanctions," he stressed, adding that the US government was working with investors who buy idle sanctioned tankers, refurbish them and use them to transport oil that is not subject to sanctions.

"We're going to move some of the ships from what I call the 'bad-guy fleet' to the 'good-guy fleet,'" Wright said. "They will not carry sanctioned oil anymore."

The US government has yet to unveil a detailed plan for shadow fleet tankers.

The proposal follows a deal that US President Donald Trump struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin this month to allow sales of Russian diesel onto global markets.

The agreement was seen as part of Trump's efforts to lower domestic fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections on November 3.

The US president also waived broad new sanctions on Russia authorized by ​a recent legislation, which targeted Moscow's energy revenues and threatened tariffs against the world's largest purchasers of Russian oil and gas.

The decision was sharply criticized by Ukraine and its European allies over concerns that it could undermine the credibility of sanctions and weaken Western economic pressure on Moscow.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Harris said that "the US sanctions carry outsized weight because of the threat [for countries and businesses] of being cut off from the US financial system."

If the US steps away from its sanctions on the shadow fleet, he argued, "the responsibility shifts to European policymakers." But they have "less effective options because of the diminished threat of severing financial ties."

Still, the expert stressed that Europe has some tools, pointing to the continent's key role in global shipping and insurance services.

"They can implement measures demanding that tankers carry legitimate and established insurance when traveling through their waters," he said, noting that it "would mean that many shadow fleet tankers could not in practice legally transport Russian oil."

Harris added that European policymakers could also pressure countries worldwide to better regulate the tankers flying their flags.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Carpenter said even if US eases some restrictions, the EU will have no choice but to continue enforcing its sanctions on these vessels.

"The vast majority of the shadow fleet traverses the Baltic Sea and exits it via the Danish Strait," he noted, adding that the EU is "uniquely positioned to board and inspect vessels moving through this key chokepoint."

But Russia has threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for interdicting and seizing Russian vessels suspected of being part of the shadow fleet.

And without US backing, Carpenter said, "it will be harder for EU countries to take on the burdens and risks of sanctions enforcement."

Braw echoed this view, saying that Ukraine's European allies will have to remain united and continue working closely with partners such as Japan, Australia and Canada. Nevertheless, she stressed that what they can achieve on their own "is far less than what they can achieve if the US is part of the team."

Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan.

For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket. The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff.

Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor.

The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one.

The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets.

The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission.

The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year.

The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads.

Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support.

In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice, a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response.

#771. Is Kylie Kelce Ready for Baby No. 5 With Jason Kelce?

Kylie Kelce—mom to daughters Wyatt, 7, Elliotte, 5, Bennett, 3, and Finnley, 19 months, with husband Jason Kelce—addressed whether she's considering expanding their family once more: "We enjoy chaos."

Kylie Kelce is not gonna lie about her thoughts on adding another player to her team.

The 34-year-old—who shares daughters Wyatt, 7, Elliotte, 5, Bennett, 3, and Finnley, 19 months, with husband Jason Kelce—weighed in on the possibility of having a fifth baby in the future.

“It’s funny,” Kylie shared on the Nov. 4 episode of her Not Gonna Lie podcast when her guest Joanna Gaines asked if she’d be open to having more kids. “That was one of the questions that we talked about.”

As a mom of five herself, Joanna—who shares kids Drake, 21, Ella, 20, Duke, 18, Emmie, 16, and Crew, 8, with husband Chip Gaines—encouraged Kylie to have one more kid.

“Five is a good number,” the Fixer Upper star noted to Kylie, who asked, “Is it?”

“And it’s gonna be a boy,” Joanna added. “I think you should do it.”

While Kylie laughed at the interior designer’s quip about the possibility of having a boy after four girls, she appeared intrigued, especially when Joanna noted that she thinks Kylie and Jason—who married in 2018—“thrive in chaos.”

“We do,” Kylie admitted. “We enjoy chaos.”

“You think one more?” the podcast host asked Joanna with a smile, to which the HGTV star  replied, “Yes, obviously, give it some time.”

“Kylie, bust it out, five,” she continued, adding further encouragement. “It’s gonna be your little boy and it's gonna rock your world because it's totally different than girls and it's another spot in your heart. Or if it's a girl, great, ‘cause five girls is a party house.”

And Kylie couldn’t help but highlight that the number five does have quite the ring to it, especially in sports terms.

After all, she noted, “It's a starting five, isn't it?”

Although the Not Gonna Lie host didn’t give a direct answer about expanding her and Jason’s team, she did make it clear that she was taking Joanna’s words to heart.

“OK, if we have a fifth child, I'm gonna come right back to this moment right here,” Kylie shared with a laugh, before joking, “‘Jo did it!’”

But Joanna ended the topic by throwing in one last play.

As she told Kylie, “Let me do the nursery!”

While time will tell what the future holds, Kylie didn’t hesitate to tackle the bodyshamers who speculated she was expecting over the summer after she shared photos from a trip to Paris.

“Stop trying to get me to have more. Stop it,” she stressed on a July 30 episode of Not Gonna Lie. “That's between me, my husband, and my motherf--king uterus.”

As she emphasized, “Even if, which I am not, even if I was with child, that is between me and my husband to decide when we would like to share that information.”

For a closer look at Kylie and Jason’s huddle of six, keep reading…

In October 2019, Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce welcomed their first baby together, a daughter named Wyatt Elizabeth Kelce.

Their second daughter Elliotte Ray Kelce joined the family two years later.

One year after Elliotte's arrival, Kylie shared that "another Kelce lady" would be added to the bunch with an adorable set of photos.

On Halloween 2022, Jason and a then-pregnant Kylie dressed up as Piglet and Kanga, respectively. Meanwhile, their girls were Tigger and Winne the Pooh.

In February 2023, the couple welcomed their third child, with her arrival coming nearly two weeks after Jason faced off against brother Travis Kelce at the 2023 Super Bowl.

Jason shared a glimpse at his oldest daughters holding a huge prize in May 2023, writing on Instagram, "Never in a million years did I think I’d hold the Larry O’Brien trophy, let alone that it would be in my house!!"

"Unbelievable honor to see it in person," he continued. "The size is incredible, looks so small when NBA players are holding it, but it’s actually massive!! The girls were very interested in it."

The family of five hit the field in August 2023, with Kylie joking in an Instagram post, "Here for the Rita’s and obstacle courses with dad after practice."

Jason and Kylie rang in Wyatt's fourth birthday in October 2023 on the Philadelphia Eagles' home turf. As Kylie noted on Instagram, "We were celebrating a 4th birthday when the Birds went 4-0."

Kylie shared this pic of Wyatt, Elliotte and Bennett on Instagram in June 2024, writing, "Parents know… 2 out of 3 isn’t bad!"

Jason's mom Donna Kelce commented, "The cutest beautiful bunch of 'lucky charms' under that rainbow!!!!"

Jason and Kylie welcomed their fourth baby girl Finnley "Finn" Anne Kelce on March 30, 2025.

Kylie craddled her Finn in her arms after the baby's March 2025 arrival.

Little Finn rocked a floral onesie shortly after she was born in the hospital.

The Philadelphia Eagles alum held newborn Finnley close in an Instagram photo shared in April 2025.

Both Liverpool and on-loan Uruguay defender Ronald Araujo plan to wait until the end of the season before deciding whether to turn the 27-year-old's move from Barcelona into a permanent switch for Â£47m. (Sport - in Spanish), external

#769. Justin Timberlake Makes Rare Appearance With Sons Silas and Phineas

Justin Timberlake attended the Global Down Syndrome Foundation's Be Beautiful Be Yourself Fashion Show alongside his and Jessica Biel’s sons Silas, 11, and Phineas, 6, Nov. 7.

Justin Timberlake and his family are shining somethin’ like a mirror.

The Grammy winner stepped out for a rare appearance with his and Jessica Biel’s sons Silas, 11, and Phineas, 6, at the Global Down Syndrome Foundation's Be Beautiful Be Yourself Fashion Show in Denver, Colorado, Nov. 7, where they were *NSYNC as they strutted down the event’s runway together.

Also bringing cuteness back to the event was Jessica’s 7-year-old niece Zaya—the daughter of Jessica’s brother Justin Biel and his wife Rose—who held onto her uncle and cousin Silas’ hands as she made her ways down the catwalk.

For the occasion, the “Mirrors” singer and his boys brought out their best suit and ties. After all, Justin and Phineas twinned in all-black ensembles while Silas looked cool as could be in black trousers, a white button-down shirt and a bomber jacket, which he accessorized with a tie and matching sunglasses.

Meanwhile, Zaya—who has Down syndrome and was honored as GLOBAL’s Ambassador at the event in 2024—also put her best fashionable foot forward in a black-and-white polka dot dress and fringe boots.

Though Jessica, 44, wasn’t pictured at the event this year, she strutted her stuff down the annual event’s runway with her niece and sons two years ago, an experience she called “truly special” at the time.

“Walking the runway with my amazing niece @lovelyzayab was an unforgettable honor,” she wrote on Instagram in November 2024. “Huge thanks to the @globaldownsyndrome foundation for creating such a profound, empowering event and for all the incredible work you do. My heart is so full.”

While Justin, 45, and Jessica are known for keeping their kiddos out the spotlight, it seems they’re slowly but surely lowering the veil on their private world. After all, Silas recently made a cameo in his mom’s Matchbox movie, where he had a small nonspeaking role towards the end of the Apple TV film.

But don’t expect the tween to score any larger roles in his mom’s films without putting in a little elbow grease.

"There are kids who work really hard, and they go to acting class and they're in theater class and they're doing all the work," Jessica recalled telling their son during her Oct. 22 appearance on the Josh Smith's Great Chat Show podcast. "You can't just take a part from that person just because you're my son. That's not cool."

Indeed, the 7th Heaven star won’t be letting her kids cut the line in front of actors who have been waiting until the end of time for their big break.

As she put it, "We're not starting like, 'Oh, you just get handed a bunch of opportunities because you're part of this family."

Keep reading for a closer look at Justin and Jessica’s life with their little ones…

See, all Jessical Biel wants Justin Timberlake to do is be her love.

"Happy Father’s Day to my spectacular husband who is one incredible dad," she wrote in a June 2025 Instagram of the father to sons Silas and Phineas. "And to all the other dads out there doing their thing. Leading with humility and vulnerability. Showin up with understanding and compassion, and always using humor to get through the hard stuff. Major respect and love to all y’all."

It appeared Silas and Phineas had that sunshine in their pockets, got that good soul in their feet. Jessica gave her Instagram followers a peek at their "family summer vibes" in an August 2025 post.

"You’re so many things to so many people," the 7th Heaven star wrote in a message for the singer's 43rd birthday in June 2024. "But to us you are THE ROCK. The rock we climb on, we lean against. The rock that shades us from the sun. And when we recline on you, as we always do, hopefully our butts will keep you eternally grounded and warm. We LOVE YOU."

Justin and Jessica's sons rocked the singer's Forget Tomorrow World Tour merch when he kicked off the concert series in April 2024.

Justin marked the his bride's 42nd birthday in March 2024 by sharing this peek at the actress hugging son Phineas.

Ain't another woman that could take her spot in Justin's life—or this March 2024 selfie.

The Grammy winner also shared this snap of The Better Sister celeb in his birthday post.

Jessica posted a sweet family snapshot as part of her Instagram tribute to Justin on Father's Day 2022.

Justin celebrated Father's Day 2022 by sharing a photo of his "two favorite melodies," sons Silas and Phineas, playing piano together.

Jessica marked her 40th birthday in 2022 with this blissed out pic.

Justin and Jessica said hi, hi, hi to a new decade, celebrating her 40th birthday with cake in 2022.

Silas and Phin marked their mom's birthday with a special banner.

"Thankful for my guys," Jessica captioned heartwarming 2021 holiday snap. "Merry Christmas everybody!!"

Jessica celebrated her "little man" on his fifth birthday in April 2020. "We’re at home, covered in legos and birthday cake right now..." she wrote in the Instagram tribute, "but I just found this pic on my phone from last summer and it made me so happy."

The Sinner actress marked her birthday on March 3, 2020 with a special cake and her one and only. "Celebrating my birthday in style... and by that I mean, in pajamas," she wrote on Instagram. "I made Justin PROMISE not to sing Happy Birthday to me, so he improvised. Sorry you can't hear it, but I'm still laughing. Thank you, you wonderful human, for really listening to me, and for throwing my kinda party. And thank YOU ALL for the birthday wishes. Feeling the love."

On Valentine's Day 2020, Jessica shared a sweet picture of Justin and their son Silas on Instagram. She captioned it, "My valentines. Love you guys to the moon."

Justin, Jessica and son Silas celebrated Fourth of July in 2019 with balloons and patriotic garb.

The trio spent Mother's Day in 2019 getting in touch with Mother Nature.

Jessica and Justin looked madly in love at her birthday party in March 2019.

The famous trio dressed up as Batman, Robin and Harley Quinn for Halloween 2018. "This Halloween was one hell of a block party!" she shared on Instagram. "Happy Halloween from our LEGO family to yours."

"They got candy? LEGO!" Justin joked of their 2018 Halloween looks.

"To my husband who I watch with awe everyday as he guides and teaches, encourages and supports, and above all, LOVES the sh$t, out of his own young man," Jessica wrote on Instagram in 2018. "Happy Father's Day to all the dads out there. We can't do this parenting thing without you."

"If that pic doesn't say ‘City Of Love' then I'm out..." Justin shared of this 2018 snap from Paris.

For Halloween in 2017, the family of three really reached for the sky with their Toy Story looks.

"Happy Halloween from Poppy, Branch and lil Branch. We be Trollin'..." Jessica wrote on Instagram after Halloween 2016.

#768. Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Bernd Leno (Fulham): Unbelievable couple of saves from him to keep Fulham in the game. I thought Newcastle should have been three or four up before Fulham got the equaliser.

Ronald Araujo (Liverpool): He is just the difference maker to that Liverpool backline. The injury-time Crystal Palace penalty that denied them a clean sheet was a terrible decision, but when he is in the team, they play better and look more solid.

Jair Cunha (Nottingham Forest): Exceptional. His goal helps, but exceptional at sniffing out the danger. Erling Haaland didn't have a sniff of a goal in Man City's defeat by Forest. Cunha will need to be really good going forward if they're the team Oliver Glasner wants.

Tarik Muharemovic (Leeds United): Many times he got caught one v one against Spurs but showed his ability to be chilled and calm under pressure and make his tackle. Very unassuming.

Nordi Mukiele (Sunderland): He was excellent again. He forced Chelsea to go wide and I think that was the key to them winning the game.

Leon Goretzka (Aston Villa): Although it was 4-4 in the end at Man Utd, Goretzka was a beast. He was calm under pressure and moved the ball really well as well. He obviously got a goal but his passing, movement and the ability to just be calm and handle every situation presented to him was really, really good.

Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool): How this guy has not got a new deal I don't know. He keeps coming up big, high energy and he is vitally important to the way Liverpool play. When he is fit and available and firing on all cylinders it feels like they have a chance in this title race.

Enzo Le Fee (Sunderland): Where would Sunderland be without this guy? He has been good, he has been scoring, chipping in with big moments. Also his ability to take the ball when under pressure, take his side up the pitch and also have that little bit of innovative play and free thinking. He is exceptional.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (Everton): Bossed the game for Everton against Coventry. Unbelievable goal but he absolutely bossed it. There was nothing more he could have done. Never gave the ball away, defensively he was solid. Attacking wise - goals and assists.

Thierno Barry (Everton): The two up front pick themselves, but probably the last time I would have them together in the same team. Did really well, two good goals against Coventry and probably should have had a third as well.

Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest): What a game for him and moment he needed. A lot of pressure from the outside, including myself. Hasn't shown up big this season but against his former team Man City, his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca as well, and he turned around and said, 'you know what, I am the man and you should have kept me around'. Scored two unbelievable goals, led the line well and looked physically fitter and stronger. Maybe now that confidence comes through and we see the best of him after the international break.

Mikel Arteta (Arsenal): I am going for Mikel Arteta simply because he has just won the Premier League. Well done. I said at the start of the season that, for me, Arsenal will win the league by 10 points and this weekend they did it. It's November and the season is officially over.

Do you agree with Troy's selections? Who would be in your Team of the Week? Have your say using the comments form below:

#767. 2 astronauts will finish upgrading ISS solar arrays during spacewalk today: Watch it live

Join The Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

The spacewalk is scheduled to start at 8:30 a.m. ET.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Two spacewalking astronauts will finish upgrading the International Space Station's power system today (Nov. 5), and you can watch the action live.

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and the Canadian Space Agency's Joshua Kutryk will install the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) today, during a roughly seven-hour spacewalk that's scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT).

You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA, beginning at 7 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT).

Today's extravehicular activity (EVA) will be the second in a week for Menon and Kutryk, who installed the station's seventh iROSA during an Oct. 29 spacewalk. That excursion was the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the ISS to date, and the first EVA for a Canadian astronaut since 2019.

Today's spacewalk will wrap up an ambitious ISS power upgrade that has taken more than five years to pull off.

"The installation job will complete the years-long process that began in June 2021 to augment the space station’s power generating capacity from 160 kilowatts to about 215 kilowatts," NASA officials wrote about the EVA in a blog post on Tuesday (Nov. 3). That's a boost of about 30%.

Menon and Kutryk are currently sharing the ISS with five other astronauts — NASA's Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov.

Delaney, Kutryk, Teteryatnikov and Watkins arrived at the ISS on Oct. 1, on SpaceX's Crew-13 mission. Dubrov, Kikina and Menon got there in mid-July, aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz. #766. Jodie Sweetin Had $190 in Her Bank Account Before Filming Fuller House

Jodie Sweetin revealed she had only $190 in her bank account before signing on for Fuller House in 2016: “Nobody that I worked with knew that.”

Jodie Sweetin is shedding light on her past financial struggles.

The Full House alum shared she fell on tough times before signing on for the sitcom’s 2016 reboot Fuller House, revealing she only had about $190 to her name at the time.

“I had to borrow money the first week I was working on Fuller House, and I [skittered] into my first paycheck with like $190 in my bank account,” Sweetin recalled on a recent episode of the We’re Still Here, Babe podcast. “And nobody that I worked with knew that.”

Since Full House wrapped in 1995, Sweetin—who played Stephanie Tanner on the show—has been open about the cycle of partying and drug use she fell into after cameras stopped rolling. And it wasn’t long until she found herself with “no money,” which forced her to find a job outside of the spotlight to make ends meet.

“I didn’t have [an] ego about it,” Sweetin explained. “I didn’t care that I was, quote, unquote, working a normal job. I think other people again were like, ‘What are you doing here?’ And I was like, ‘Paying my bills. Kids don’t pay for themselves.’”

That’s why Sweetin—who shares daughters Zoie, 18, with ex-husband Cody Herpin and Beatrix, 16, with ex Morty Coyle—spent her days as a logistics coordinator at a treatment center in Los Angeles before returning to TV.

At the time, she lived in a one-and-a-half-bedroom apartment with her two kids, sharing she made $2,200 a month.

But in knowing what she does now, Sweetin says she wouldn’t trade her less-than-glamorous chapter for the world.

“Not like I was ever a materialistic person,” Sweetin explained, “but you learn humility when you are at Target and you’ve got to turn around and, you know, put some s--t back, because you don’t have the money on your debit card.”

But even as she was experiencing her financial struggles, Sweetin “learned to be really happy” with her life.

“I was like, ‘I would be fine doing this. If this is what I’m going to do, cool,’” she said. “And I just threw myself into being as fully present as I could be and that old ‘bloom where you’re planted’ kind of vibe.”

“Like, if this is what it is, then I’m going to make it good,” she added, “and I’m going to have fun, and I’m going to enjoy it.”

Indeed, she wasn’t about to spend her time wishing for a “bigger” life. As she put it, “That’s bulls--t.”

Keep reading for more celebs who have taken up jobs outside of showbiz…

The Catfish host obtained his salesperson license in New York and announced in September 2025 he had begun to work as a real estate agent at Coldwell Banker Warburg to follow in the footsteps of his dad, a longtime broker at the company.

While Jon & Kate Plus 8 alum Kate Gosselin lamented the fact that so much of her savings went toward paying lawyers in her battle with ex-husband Jon Gosselin, the evidence would suggest she's enjoyed her return to nursing.

"I am an RN, I work in PEDs home health care,” Kate detailed in an August 2025 TikTok. “I work with one family currently. The patients already know my name and some things about me so before I come into their home, they know who I am. And I imagine they already know me."

What she knows, though, is that helping others is quite fulfilling.

"It’s actually been a really rewarding and fun job," Kate continued. "To come in and relieve a family of their medically challenged child so that they can spend time with their other kids and do other things."

For Drew Barrymore, a day of work has never been missed. Though her current gig helming The Drew Barrymore Show fills her days now, when the child star found herself emancipated from mom Jaid Barrymore at age 14, she scrambled to pay the bills.

Noting her friend worked at a coffee shop in the Valley, the actress shared in her 2015 memoir Wildflower that she had to find something closer to their rental because she didn't have a driver's license.

"It was the start of the 1990s, and coffeehouses were where everyone hung out," she detailed of working at L.A. hot spot the Living Room. "People poured out on to the street every night." Unfortunately, she continued, "I wasn’t great at my job. I wasn't really great at anything. I had only done two things: acted and had wild life experiences."

She served up the tea on one tense experience in her book.

"I could tell my boss, who had hired me on the novel idea of having a washed-up former child actor behind the counter, was patient with all my learning curves, but was also irritated with me," she wrote, revealing how he walked in while she was doing the dishes "and said, very sharply and exasperatedly, 'Don't use the abrasive side of the brush! All the pastry cases are getting scratched and foggy, and you can't see what’s inside!'"

Yep, Love Island USA alum Leah Kateb has an office job. In July 2025, she became the Chief Creative Officer for the fragrance company Skylar, describing herself as a "re-founder" of the brand.

When Stranger Things' Noah Schnapp isn't battling supernatural beings in the Upside Down, he spends his time saving others in another way. In a 2022 interview with Flaunt magazine, the actor revealed he had a part time job as a lifeguard at his local pool during the summer.

"It's kind of a 'just for fun thing,'" he explained. "I've kind of grown up with a normal life and normal friends and stuff outside of Stranger Things, so it's kind of kept me grounded."

In the late '90s and early '00s, Erik von Detten captured the hearts of teens everywhere thanks to his roles in Escape to Witch Mountain, Brink! and The Princess Diaries. But after last acting credit in 2010 (a voiceover in Toy Story 3), von Detten's career trajectory took a turn, landing him in the financial industry.

"Simultaneously when things started to slow down in acting in my early 20s, another opportunity presented itself for me with a company that I started working with at age 25," von Detten shared in a rare interview with E! in 2021. "And I've been with that company ever since. It's a sales position with a company working in finance. I've grown into a management position and it's worked out really well."

Several years after starring in the 2007 movie adaptation of Hairspray, Golden Globe nominee Nikki Blonsky made headlines when it was reported she was working as a makeup artist at a beauty salon on Long Island.

"Its true Im workin@ Superstar Salon as a makeup artist & more Im proud 2 b workin & helpin pay bills," Blonsky wrote on X (formerly Twitter) in 2011. "BUT ill NEVER loose sight of my dreams."

After starring as California Highway Patrol officer Ponch on TV series CHiPs, which ran from 1977 to 1983, Erik Estrada went on to become a reserve police officer for the Muncie Police Department in Indiana. The actor later moved to Virginia, where he worked as an investigator for the I.C.A.C. (Internet Crimes Against Children) before once again working as a reserve police officer in St. Anthony, Idaho in 2016.

Ethan Craft serving as your real estate agent? That's what dreams are made of!

Lizzie McGuire heartthrob Clayton Snyder chose not to pursue a career in acting after the Disney Channel series ended. Why? He wanted to focus on water polo, later playing for California's Pepperdine University.

"Frankly, when the show wrapped up, I was kind of thankful," Snyder admitted to E! News in 2022. "I was like, 'Okay, phew, going into high school, new chapter, that's done. We're going to see what this is going to be like.'"

Snyder now works in real estate in Los Angeles, though his past as a child star does occasionally come up.

"I would really like it to be you want to work with me because I'm really good at what I do and if it's a nice piece of trivia that I'm 'that guy' then that's wonderful," he said. "We've had plenty of clients of where halfway through showing them homes they're like, 'My wife and I just found out who you are and we can't believe it!' But that makes me feel good because I know that's not why they're working with me."

We bet you didn't know that the oldest Jonas Brother owned and operated his own construction company in New Jersey during The Jonas Brothers' eight-year hiatus? Plus, Kevin Jonas also became the co-CEO of The Blu Market, an influencer marketing company.

Child actor Charlie Korsmo, known for his turn in Hook and the teen drama Can't Hardly Wait, left Hollywood behind to become a lawyer. And now, he is also a professor of corporate law and corporate finance at the Case Western Reserve University School of Law in Cleveland.

President Barack Obama nominated Korsmo as a member of the Board of Trustees of the Barry Goldwater Scholarship and Excellence in Education Foundation in 2011.

Yep, Charlie gave up the chocolate factory.

Peter Ostrum made his acting debut as Charlie Bucket in 1971's Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory, which would ultimately be his only onscreen role. After graduating from Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine in 1984, Ostrum went on to become a veterinarian.

Wizards of Waverly Place scenestealer Jennifer Stone traded in her character Harper Finkle's funky wardrobe for a pair of scrubs when she became a registered nurse in 2019. The former Disney Channel actress then joined the health care workers who are on the front lines fighting against coronavirus.

"A very good friend of mine (@maiarawalsh ) pointed out to me that today is #worldhealthday . It is also the day I went from a volunteer, then a student nurse, and now an RN resident," Stone shared on Instagram in 2020. "I just hope to live up to all of the amazing healthcare providers on the front lines now as I get ready to join them."

Former child star Ross Bagley, known for his roles as Buckwheat in The Little Rascals and Nicky Banks on The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, now works as a real estate agent in Los Angeles.

So long, Truffle Shuffle, hello, habeus corpus.

After playing Chunk in the classic '80s movie The Goonies, Jeff Cohen quit acting to become an attorney, working as an entertainment lawyer in Los Angeles.

After his one-season stint as the brooding Duncan Kane on Veronica Mars, Teddy Dunn became a lawyer and served as an Assistant United States Attorney at the United States Attorney's Office District of Columbia.

Known for her breakout turn (and pool exit) in The Fast Times at Ridgemont High, as well as her roles in Gremlins and Drop Dead Fred, Phoebe Cates left the acting world behind in the '90s after welcoming two children with her husband, actor Kevin Kline.

Cates went on to open Blue Tree, a gift boutique on New York City's Madison Avenue, in 2005.

Following his time as Nevel on the popular Nickelodeon series iCarly, Reed Alexander went on to become a journalist, working for outlets such as Business Insider and the Wall Street Journal.

Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor—encapsulated within a GalNAc–lipid nanoparticle—leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

#764. 'Tinkerman' Alonso's Chelsea side still searching for identity

Struggling Sunderland get a narrow win at home against Chelsea

Constant changes in formation and personnel - and another disappointing defeat.

Xabi Alonso's frustration was obvious as Chelsea's struggles for identity continued in the 1-0 defeat by Sunderland.

It is starting to feel as though the Spaniard is the latest "Tinkerman" at Stamford Bridge, a moniker first associated with Blues boss Claudio Ranieri back in 2002-03.

For the first time this season, Chelsea lined up with a three-man midfield - but they were also without a recognised striker for the second match in a row, with Pedro Neto again struggling to lead the line in their loss at the Stadium of Light.

By contrast, struggling Sunderland were led by target man Brian Brobbey, who won a 36th-minute penalty after being brought down by Levi Colwill. Enzo le Fee converted the game's only goal from the spot.

That decision came moments after Chelsea were denied a penalty when Cole Palmer went down under a challenge from Luke O'Nien, but the video assistant referee ruled that contact had started outside the box.

Those two incidents in quick succession meant Alonso and his coaching staff appeared angry on the touchline after the Sunderland goal.

However, the Chelsea manager refused to criticise the officials after the game - instead he gave brief answers that changed the subject and were critical towards his players for not carrying out the gameplan properly.

Asked whether Brobbey was simply unstoppable, Alonso, 44, replied: "No, he's stoppable. He's stoppable, but we have to do it better than we did today.

"Out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances. He got the penalty as well.

"I'm not happy with how we defended that situation. It's something that we could have avoided, something that we had worked on during the week. To concede penalties is not good for us."

It left nowhere to hide for Colwill, who was substituted at half-time, with Moises Caicedo filling in at centre-back despite having barely completed a full training session all week and needing careful management of his own fitness issues.

Chelsea also created few clear chances, aside from a headed opportunity that Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers squandered, while Palmer also struggled - days after being left out of the England squad.

Before the season started, Alonso said he wanted his Chelsea side to be "unpredictable".

Although factors such as injuries are beyond his control, his side have achieved that, but to their own detriment.

Failed to deal with Brobbey - player ratings for Sunderland v Chelsea

Sunderland beat Chelsea for first league win since August

Chelsea have five wins, four losses and a draw in 10 Premier League games under Xabi Alonso

Only Tottenham (28) have made more more line-up changes than Chelsea (24) in the Premier League this season.

In the early part of the campaign, they at least had a settled and exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Rogers and Palmer.

It was largely the reason behind the positive start to the season despite failing to keep a clean sheet against top-flight opposition until Alonso's eighth game in charge.

With Caicedo injured, they suffered problems in midfield and continued to make changes from match to match, while also experimenting with personnel to fix the defence.

However, they largely looked on course to emulate the back-three system Alonso excelled with during his historic German double-winning season at Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24.

As Caicedo returned after the international break, however, captain Reece James was injured.

Joao Pedro featured in wins against Bournemouth and Everton before sustaining a thigh injury, having already missed Brazil's international matches.

Number one goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez broke his jaw in a collision at Everton, while Maxence Lacroix, who had been a near ever-present since joining from Crystal Palace in the summer, is expected to be out until January with a hamstring injury.

Defender Jorrel Hato has also suffered a setback in recent weeks.

It has left Alonso reacting to events when selecting his starting XI, with the Spaniard saying: "There are situations. Yesterday Josh [Acheampong] said he was not ready to play, so we are short of options and we need to walk through this step.

"Even when we win, when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting for them to come back because they are important."

He admitted his side were missing Joao Pedro, although supporters have also been frustrated that Estevao Willian, who came on at half-time on Sunday, has started only one league match this season.

Prior to Sunday's game, Chelsea were averaging just 46% possession. They then dominated the ball at Sunderland (with 68.7% possession) but without creating many significant chances.

Meanwhile, only Crystal Palace have conceded more shots on target than Chelsea's 50, while the Blues top the league with 53 shots on target - meaning there have been plenty of chances at both ends during their matches.

Alonso can still be pleased with Chelsea having collected five more points than they managed from the equivalent fixtures last season, with the club on course to qualify for the Champions League while sitting fifth in the table.

However, that is a low bar after a dismal campaign last season, when Chelsea finished 10th.

Going into the November international break, Alonso remains a long way from establishing a style of play, or an identity capable of bringing consistency - although he promised promising in an interview last week that Chelsea would be "different" and "better" by the end of the season.

#762. Dorgu makes dramatic impact - Man Utd v Aston Villa ratings

Patrick Dorgu rises to head Manchester United's injury-time equaliser in a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa

Manchester United fought back from two goals twice to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa as Patrick Dorgu made a dramatic impact off the bench.

But who impressed and who didn't in the Old Trafford epic?

Senne Lammens: One of Man Utd's best performers this season but a calamitous start to this one. First goal went straight through him and he spilled a shot straight from Nicolas Jackson for the second. Went wrong way for penalty too. 4

Diogo Dalot (off 66, Dorgu): Got his body in the right position to close half the goal off for the opener but was in the wrong position to make challenge on Alysson at start of second half to gift Villa a penalty. 4

Leny Yoro: Moved back into the centre, intelligently stepped up to win the ball on halfway, then spoiled good work by attempting a lofted pass when Matheus Cunha wanted it on the ground. Almost headed into his own net in build-up to Villa's fourth goal. 5

Harry Maguire (off 46, Heaven): Managed to clear his head quickly enough to lead United's defence after their shocking start. A doubt pre-match, he went off at half-time. 5

Noussair Mazraoui: Struggled along with many others this season. Asked to push forward, which he seems to find easier for his country but not his club. 4

Youri Tielemans (off 66, Mount): Baited by the Aston Villa fans given his Â£35m summer move from them, but answered in the best way by driving home an equaliser for his first United goal. 6

Kobbie Mainoo: Threatened with a long-range effort and nearly picked out Amad Diallo's run with a precise chipped pass over the visitors defence. 6

Amad Diallo (off 66, Lacey): Kept his place ahead of crowd favourite Shea Lacey but one chase back into his own box showed why, defensively, it made sense. Came close to an equaliser and should have ended an 11-month wait for a goal but Zion Suzuki saved well. 6

Bruno Fernandes: For the second game running, he kept his cool to covert from the spot when the pressure was at its highest. Looked unhappy at the end despite the comeback. 7

Matheus Cunha: Driving run into the visiting box brought a crucial penalty. Curling effort was heading for the corner but turned around post by Suzuki. United's most dangerous attacker. 7

Bryan Mbeumo (off 83, Zirkzee): Did a lot of chasing in the first half to try to pressure the Villa defence into mistakes. 6

Ayden Heaven (on 46, Maguire): Booked for late tackle on Alysson after being introduced at break. 6

Mason Mount (on 66, Tielemans): Hit the bar with first time shot but sliced later effort over. 6

Shea Lacey (on 66, Amad): Tried to create. 6

Patrick Dorgu (on 66 Dalot): What an ending as he changed the outcome of the game with an assist and goal. 8

Joshua Zirkzee (on 83, Mbeumo): Scored in stoppage time and goal proved crucial. 6

Subs not used: Darlow, De Ligt, Andrey Santos, J Fletcher.

Premier League: Man Utd score twice in stoppage time to draw with Villa but stay in drop zone

Zion Suzuki: Kept busy as the hosts hunted an equaliser. One excellent save from Cunha and a couple when he benefited from a kind rebound, but bad error for United's late equaliser. 5

Victor Lindelof: Found himself under a lot of pressure on a ground he knows so well and turned in an accomplished performance. 7

Taylor Harwood-Bellis: Had to remain concentrated and wasn't faultless but emerged with credit in the bank. 6

Pau Torres: Guided a header over as Villa attacked but biggest task was trying to stop Cunha. As it turned out, a stride too late getting out when Tielemans scored. Couldn't keep United out in the end. 6

Ian Maatsen: Testing day, trying to stop Amad attacking and looking to beat Mazraoui at the other end. Was doing well until the late drama. 7

Alysson (off 71, Barkley): Even the Brazilian must have been a little bit surprised his first-minute shot ended up in the net. His shot created the second and came so close to adding another to his tally after being released by Goretzka. Won the penalty at start of second half too. 8

Boubacar Kamara: Ill-advised attempted tackle on Cunha led to penalty that offered the hosts a way back into the game. Struggled to contain the home attack. 7

John McGinn (off 71, Hemmings): Everything looked so good in the opening minutes but then had to try to ensure Villa didn't fall apart as United fought back. Kept his concentration to score from the spot and created panic with a free-kick. 7

Leon Goretzka (off 78, Mbaye): Tried to relieve pressure on Villa defence as the hosts fought back and drove home Villa's fourth on a crazy day. 7

Johan Manzambi (off 78, Gomes): Not the easiest game for the Swiss international to shine given its general chaotic nature. Tried to get control but no real chance of that. 5

Nicolas Jackson (off 86, Madjo): Alert to snaffle home the rebound after Lammens had spilled McGinn's shot. Not the best performance but much effective than in his Chelsea days. 7

George Hemmings (on 71, McGinn): Came on to shore things up but move didn't work. 5

Ross Barkley (on 71, Alysson): Won't remember ending with fondness. 5

Subs not used: Bizot, Mings, Buendia, Cisse.

#761. Are 'outstanding' Brighton now Arsenal's main title challengers?

Brighton have won six of their last seven Premier League matches

Few, if any, Brighton supporters could have anticipated just how impressive their side would be during the opening 10 games of the Premier League season.

A 2-0 victory over Brentford at the Amex Stadium on Sunday afternoon lifted the Seagulls into second place, leaving them to head into the November international break dreaming of what might be possible over the remainder of the campaign.

Their sixth win in seven Premier League matches was enough to move them above Manchester City, who suffered a shock 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest less than 24 hours earlier, and underline their position as the closest challengers to leaders Arsenal.

With a five-point gap to the Gunners, that is certainly the case for now, although Brighton's influential midfielder Pascal Gross was reluctant to entertain such talk at this stage.

"No, we are not in a title race," the 35-year-old told Sky Sports after Sunday's success.

"But we have started the season really well. It's the beginning of the season.

"You see the Premier League, the margins and you look at the results - we are not getting carried away yet.

"Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum, but we are really pleased to head into the international break like this."

But 10 years on from Leicester City's title triumph against all odds, could they really achieve the impossible and win the Premier League?

Gross has made more than 290 appearances across two spells at Brighton

As each week passes, though, it is becoming increasingly difficult to dismiss Brighton's credentials.

Having won seven of their opening 10 Premier League matches, including beating Arsenal and Manchester City, the Seagulls have shown quality as well as character.

But it is not just their league position that makes for impressive reading. Almost all of the underlying numbers point to a side capable of maintaining their early-season form.

Brighton have created the second-highest number of big chances (37) in the division and scored more goals (26) than any other side this term.

Much of their attacking threat has been driven by Gross, who rejoined the club from Borussia Dortmund in January, having left in 2024.

The German midfielder has spent seven-and-a-half years at the Amex across two spells, either side of his spell back in his homeland, and has re-established himself as Brighton's creative heartbeat this season.

Gross has created eight big chances in the Premier League, more than any other player.

As well as finding the back of the net against Brentford, he also created at least five chances for his team-mates.

It was the 27th time since the start of the 2017-18 season that Gross has created five or more chances in a single match, with only Kevin de Bruyne (48) and Bruno Fernandes (47) having managed more.

He admitted earlier this week: "I just keep going. I think I'm fit, I try to prepare as good as I can and try to help the team win games."

At the other end of the pitch, only defending champions and current leaders Arsenal have been more impressive than Brighton, who have kept the joint-highest number of clean sheets (seven) and conceded the second-fewest goals (five) in the division.

"The way they're playing at the moment, Champions League qualification is probably the minimum that you'd expect Brighton to achieve," former Everton midfielder Leon Osman told BBC Sport.

"They look like a team that has really kicked on over the last 18 months. The football they're playing is outstanding and they are a great team to watch.

"Can they win the league? I think it would be unexpected if they did, but I expected them to win something this year, whether that is a domestic trophy like the FA Cup or the Conference League."

There was another welcome boost for Brighton as Yankuba Minteh made his first Premier League appearance of the season against Brentford.

The Gambia forward, who was the subject of an unsuccessful bid from Liverpool during the summer, has been one of their most dangerous attacking players since joining from Newcastle United in 2024.

Minteh's return to fitness is expected to be followed closely by that of Kaoru Mitoma, who has been sidelined since May with a hamstring complaint.

Arsenal have won nine of their 10 Premier League games this season, losing only to Brighton

There is a feeling an opportunity could be seized in the title race this season.

Although Arsenal have won nine of their opening 10 matches, they have arguably not been quite as convincing as they were during their title-winning campaign last season and were beaten 3-0 at Brighton in September.

Elsewhere, Manchester City fell further behind with a third successive league defeat on Saturday evening at the City Ground.

But even if Enzo Maresca's side were to rediscover their form after the international break - and visit Arsenal on 29 November - there remains considerable uncertainty over how their season could unfold following their financial charges.

City were found guilty of breaching 114 Premier League financial rules by an independent commission earlier this year, three-and-a-half years after they were first charged by the league.

The club have since exercised their right to appeal the verdict and vehemently deny any wrongdoing.

However, should they fail in their appeal, City could face a significant points deduction or, in the most extreme scenario, expulsion from the Premier League.

Were that to happen, Brighton would, based on the current standings, emerge as Arsenal's most realistic title challengers.

In fourth and fifth spot are Liverpool and Chelsea, the only two sides to have beaten Brighton in the league this season. But they appear to be enduring transitional campaigns and are currently a significant way off the pace required to mount a challenge.

Osman believed it was the perfect opportunity for Brighton to take advantage as he added: "They have taken time to build this team, letting some of their best players go and redoing the whole thing all over again.

"Now they just seem to be getting to a point where they'll be keeping their best players.

"They are in this great position where it is now time to get the most out of all this ability for their own success, to benefit the club and the fans, rather than just for the financial gain of selling players on for huge profits."

#760. Live Tinted’s Founder Shares Her Secret to a "Luminous" Diwali Glow

E! exclusively spoke with Deepica Mutyala, founder of Live Tinted, about how to achieve a "luminous" glow for Diwali, and how she formulates her unique & purposeful products.

Live Tinted made history just over 5 years ago at Ulta Beauty when they became the first South Asian-founded makeup brand to launch there, and recently came together for a special Diwali celebration.

Following her star-studded event, E! spoke exclusively with founder Deepica Mutyala about her partnership with Ulta, the best products to get a luminous Diwali glow, plus her commitment to purposeful formulas and inclusive shade ranges.

Deepica shared, "It's honestly such a full-circle moment! When we launched at Ulta Beauty in 2021 as its first South Asian-founded makeup brand, it was a milestone I never could have imagined growing up. Five years later, we're one of Ulta's fastest-growing prestige cosmetics brands!"

"Hosting one of the beauty industry's largest Diwali celebrations alongside Ulta's leadership this year was incredibly meaningful. Seeing nearly 200 people from across beauty, fashion, and entertainment come together to celebrate my culture reminded me just how far we've come and what's possible for the next generation of founders," she added.

#759. Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown

The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.

The company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September. One-off costs, not least a massive writedown in its stake in struggling sister company Porsche, explained the vast bulk of the losses.

The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.

It is pursuing a major restructuring and downsizing program, trying to bolster falling profit margins, and executives said the difficulties highlighted the urgency of this process.

"The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act quickly and decisively," chief financial officer Arno Antlitz said in a video statement.

The results were the latest reminder of the pressure on VW — and the wider German and Western automotive industry — to react to increasing competition in China, high costs and practical difficulties moving towards electric car production, and unpredictable and rising tariff burdens, thanks in no small part to US President Donald Trump.

And here are some of the key year-to-date 9-month figures:

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

VW shares were already at their lowest levels in well over 10 years prior to Thursday's announcements, after months of difficult headlines and the ongoing plans to shed tens of thousands of jobs and reduce production capacities.

Perhaps as a result of this, the stock dipped briefly as markets opened and the news was published, but then started to rally as the day progressed.

By midday in Frankfurt, VW shares had climbed by 2% compared to their prices at the start of trading on the DAX.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

CEO Oliver Blume plans to shed around 100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands, in the coming years though a combination of layoffs and not replacing departing or retiring personnel.

Multiple factors are contributing to this. They include increased competition from Chinese manufacturers, falling revenues in China, changeable US auto tariffs under President Donald Trump, different staffing requirements when manufacturing electric cars and difficulties moving towards making and selling more electric cars at the pace once designated by political leaders.

Up to four plants in Germany could face closure as part of the plan, which has met with considerable union resistance and could lead to strikes starting next year.

CFO Antlitz said the figures showed the urgency underlying these plans, saying the company needed to increase its profit margins by 2030 to solidify its finances.

Antlitz said the operating return on sales was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off writedowns hitting the bottom line.

"That is not enough in the long term," he said.

As part of its restructuring program, the VW Group aims to restore an operating profit margin of between 8-10% by 2030.

This year, amid one-off costs now totaling in the region of €10 billion, it expects a profit margin of no more than 1%, compared to prior forecasts in the region of 5%.

The Chinese roadmap includes an uncrewed lunar landing in 2028.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

China has given us some details about the epic moon landing it plans to pull off a few years from now.

Chinese officials laid out the roadmap for its crewed lunar campaign at the 7th Manned Space Symposium, which was held Oct. 31 and Nov. 1 in Beijing. The campaign consists of four missions, culminating in a crewed touchdown "before 2030," according to media reports.

That timeline — which is consistent with previous statements made by the China Manned Space Agency — keeps the pressure on the U.S., which aims to put its own astronauts down on the moon in 2028, via NASA's Artemis program.

Leaked slide confirms the four-mission progression toward China’s crewed lunar landing: 🚀2027: Maiden flight of Long March 10A carrying Mengzhou CSS cargo resupply mission, to validate the new human-rated vehicle and Mengzhou’s orbital operations in LEO. 🚀2028: First flight of the heavier CZ-10 with an uncrewed Lanyue lander performing a lunar descent and ascent test, exercising the lander’s propulsion and guidance. 🚀🚀2029: Dual CZ-10 launches of Mengzhou and Lanyue for a full-scale lunar-orbit rehearsal, demonstrating rendezvous, docking, and integrated operations. 🚀🚀Before the end of 2030: Dual CZ-10 crewed lunar landing mission.November 1, 2026

The first mission in China's four-part lunar campaign is scheduled to fly in 2027, according to CNSpaceflight, an X account that keeps a close eye on China's activities in space. The outlet cited an X user who shared a presentation slide of the plan.

That launch — the first of of China's new Long March 10A rocket — will send an uncrewed Mengzhou spacecraft to low Earth orbit (LEO) for a series of tests. Mengzhou, whose name means "Dream Vessel," is the next-gen crew capsule that will carry Chinese astronauts to lunar orbit.

Mission number two, launching in 2028, will involve a different set of hardware — the more powerful Long March 10 rocket and the Lanyue ("Embracing the Moon") lunar lander. This will also be an uncrewed flight, and it will mark the debut of the Long March 10, which will send Lanyue to orbit around the moon. If all goes to plan, Lanyue will touch down on the moon and then launch itself back to lunar orbit.

Mission number three, flying in 2029, will also target an uncrewed lunar landing, but it will feature two Long March 10 launches — one apiece for Mengzhou and Lanyue. The two spacecraft will conduct a rendezvous and docking rehearsal in lunar orbit, then separate for Lanyue's trip down to the surface.

This will set the stage for mission four — the real deal, in which two Long March 10s launch a crewed Mengzhou and an uncrewed Lanyue "before 2030." The two vessels will dock in lunar orbit, and the astronauts will move into Lanyue for their historic lunar landing.

Three astronauts will apparently launch on Mengzhou, and two of them will land on the moon aboard Lanyue, according to CNSpaceflight. The duo will spend three days on the lunar surface, conducting moonwalks on each of those days.

And about that "before 2030" timeline: The wording may have been chosen very carefully.

"One reading is that 2029 coincides with the 80th anniversary of the current government, creating a strong internal incentive to achieve the landing that year. At the same time, the technical schedule (new Long March 10 family, Mengzhou, Lanyue, dual-launch operations) remains aggressive; committing publicly to 2029 would create significant political exposure if any major test slips," CNSpaceflight wrote in a Nov. 2 X post.

"Using 'before 2030' therefore functions as deliberate wording flexibility: a 2029 landing can still be presented as an early historic success, while a slip into 2030 remains inside the stated goal without requiring a formal target revision. You just need to put 'year-end' after 'before 2030,'" the outlet added.

NASA's Artemis program has already sent astronauts around the moon, doing so this past April on the Artemis II mission. The agency is currently gearing up for Artemis III, a crewed flight to LEO that will test rendezvous and docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's two private crewed landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon.

Artemis III is currently on track to fly in the summer of 2027, NASA officials have said. But an on-time liftoff is far from guaranteed, as both Starship and Blue Moon still have some boxes to check.

Starship just reached Earth orbit for the first time on Sept. 28, for example, and it has yet to demonstrate off-Earth refueling, which will be a crucial part of any Starship mission beyond Earth orbit. And Blue Moon has yet to leave the ground at all. The Blue Origin lander is scheduled to fly for the first time next spring, on an uncrewed test mission that will send it to the lunar surface.

If all goes well on Artemis III, NASA will be clear to start prepping for Artemis IV, which will put astronauts down near the lunar south pole aboard either Starship or Blue Moon. (It's unclear at the moment which lander NASA will choose.)

NASA is currently targeting early 2028 for the launch of Artemis IV. If that schedule holds, the agency will beat China and pull off the first crewed lunar landing since Apollo 17 back in 1972.

But the new moon race won't end there, because this one isn't all about flags and footprints. Both NASA and China aim to build bases on the lunar surface over the next decade or so, setting up humanity's first true outpost on a world beyond Earth. The stakes are high, NASA and U.S. military officials have stressed: Whoever does so first can claim the best spots and get the best access to key lunar resources such as water ice. The leader will also get to establish norms of behavior on the moon, which at the moment is a bit of a Wild West of exploration.

#757. Palace consider replacing Sage, with Frank among contenders

Liverpool dispatch Palace to pile pressure on Sage

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage is in serious danger of losing his job only five months into his reign, with the club bottom of the Premier League going into the international break.

Sunday's 3-1 defeat by Liverpool was Palace's fourth successive league loss, with Sage's side having won just two of their 10 league matches this season.

The club have held internal talks aimed at deciding Sage's future and his potential successor.

Former Tottenham and Brentford manager Thomas Frank is viewed as a strong candidate, while ex-Nottingham Forest boss Sean Dyche also has some support internally.

Both are out of work and would be available to start immediately.

Palace have taken just seven points from their 10 league matches and have the worst defensive record in the league, having conceded 24 goals.

They are also 21st in the Europa League, currently enough for a play-off spot, with only one win from their four matches.

If he is dismissed, Frenchman Sage could become the first managerial casualty of the Premier League season.

He was appointed on a three-year contract in June after Oliver Glasner departed at the end of last season.

"It's not from the dream to the nightmare," the 47-year-old said after the defeat by Liverpool.

"I'm not feeling this. I'm just in my job, and focusing on my job, and what I have to do to find the solution.

"The results are not at this level, and I know I have to push more on those things, especially in our way of playing, to make that move."

Sage previously led Lens to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 and a first French Cup triumph in their 120-year history.

However, he has been unable to replicate Glasner's success at Palace. Glasner, who now manages Nottingham Forest, led Palace to a first FA Cup title and a Europa Conference League triumph.

Palace are winless in the league since 11 October, with their losing run sparked by a 5-0 loss to fierce rivals Brighton.

After that match, Sage said he felt "shame" and admitted he did not know if he would be given time to turn Palace's fortunes around.

However, there was a degree of sympathy from some behind the scenes.

Injuries were not kind to his plans, while the absence of Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr - due to a mixture of fitness and personal issues, related to both players' desire to leave the club - did not help the start of his reign.

However, three more league defeats have followed, with Palace hitting the bar and having a goal ruled out in their loss to Liverpool at Selhurst Park.

"We have to be more competitive," Sage said on Sunday.

"At the moment, we create some things, we expect a lot of things, but we don't have the results expected."

Palace's next Premier League match is at Coventry on 21 November following the two-week international break.

"This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

NASA has revealed a glimpse of its next X-plane, known as the X-70 Fractal.

Or at least what it thinks the X-70 will look like once built. The agency released a short statement on Wednesday (Nov. 4) announcing the X-plane, or experimental plane, declaring it to be a highly maneuverable test bed with a "rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology," allowing NASA to swap both external and internal components on-the-fly. This modular architecture will allow NASA to "explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight," according to the agency's statement.

The announcement was made alongside an AI-generated image showing two canted vertical tail fins emerging from swirling smoke. Little can be gleaned from the image about what final form the X-70 might take, but the tail fins are somewhat reminiscent of the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor or Boeing F/A-18 Super Hornet.

"The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in the statement. The NASA chief called the aircraft "just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics" and said that the agency expects the X-70 to make its first flight within two years.

"This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly," Isaacman added.

NASA's statement fleshes out a few details about the X-70's capabilities. According to the agency, Fractal will fly at a cruise speed of Mach .75, about the same as a Boeing 737 Classic. The X-70 will be able to reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet (13.7 kilometers), and will have a range exceeding 1,726 miles (2,777 kilometers, or 1,500 nautical miles).

The X-70 Fractal will also be able to carry around 2,000 pounds (900 kg) of experimental payloads both internally and externally, which will allow for a "wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities," NASA said in the statement.

NASA adds it will have a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds (4,535 kilograms), around the same weight as the Scaled Composites- and Northrop Grumman-developed Model 437 Vanguard experimental aircraft. In fact, the two aircraft share a similar silhouette — at least in the AI image of the X-70 Fractal NASA has released so far.

The agency's most recent X-plane, the X-59, has been flying for over a year. That jet features a radical long-nosed geometry without a forward windscreen; pilots fly by way of an augmented reality screen that combines views from sensors and a forward-facing camera.

That geometry dampens the shockwaves coming off of the X-59 when it flies faster than the sound barrier, allowing it to fly at speeds over Mach 1 without the thunderous sonic booms that typically accompany supersonic flight.

There are numerous experimental aircraft being developed by private companies, such as Boom Supersonic's X-1 jet, which, like the X-59, aims to develop technologies that lessen the auditory impact of sonic booms on the ground.

In terms of other government X-plane projects, Boeing is working on the F-47, a next-generation stealth fighter for use by the U.S. military, and DARPA, the Pentagon's research agency, has an X-plane project of its own known as CRANE.

Brett is curious about emerging aerospace technologies, alternative launch concepts, military space developments and uncrewed aircraft systems. Brett's work has appeared on Scientific American, The War Zone, Popular Science, the History Channel, Science Discovery and more. Brett has degrees from Clemson University and the University of North Carolina at Charlotte. In his free time, Brett enjoys skywatching throughout the dark skies of the Appalachian mountains.
